mainTopic: Why the משנה lists extra cases, the three opinions on decrees after חליצה and ביאה, and the new פרק's rule that any ביאה with a יבמה acquires her, including what 'forced' means.
overview: The גמרא first asks why the משנה lists a גט after חליצה, since only a מאמר after חליצה seems to teach something new. It answers that the בעילה half of the משנה has the same issue, so the extra cases are there only to keep the two halves parallel (אַיְּידֵי). Next it notes that our משנה, which says nothing works after חליצה at any stage, disagrees with a ברייתא of אבא יוסי בן יוחנן. That ברייתא treats חליצה like בעילה. This gives three opinions: the תנא קמא decrees only for ביאה, רבי נחמיה makes no decree at all, and אבא יוסי בן חנן decrees for both. The פרק רבן גמליאל then closes with a הדרן. A new פרק opens with a משנה teaching that any ביאה with a יבמה acquires her, whatever anyone intended, and that any ביאה with an ערוה or a פסולה disqualifies her. The גמרא explains the word 'אפילו' and brings רבי חייא's ברייתא, which widens the rule. It then asks what 'forced' means. Being forced by non-Jews is rejected because of רבא's rule, and the 'asleep' answer is challenged with a statement of רב יהודה that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: חליצה followed by other actions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the start of the משנה's list of actions done after חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if he did חליצה and then made a מאמר, or gave a גט, etc. (nothing takes effect after חליצה).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting a line from the משנה so it can discuss it. This is a setup line for the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה taught that once the יבם does חליצה, nothing he does afterward (מאמר, גט, or בעילה) has any effect. The 'etc.' points to the rest of that list.

keyTerms.meaning: He performed חליצה, the ceremony that releases the יבמה from יבום
A יבום-style betrothal (קידושין) made by the יבם with the יבמה
A bill of divorce
Etc.: the rest of the quote continues

phrases.english: He performed חליצה and made a מאמר, and gave, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה. The full line ends: after חליצה, nothing takes effect.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the discussion by citing the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After חליצה, no further action (מאמר, גט, בעילה) takes effect.

steps.title: Why does the משנה need the case of a גט after חליצה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא grants that 'מאמר after חליצה' teaches something new, but asks what 'גט after חליצה' adds.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that the משנה needed to teach 'he did חליצה and then a מאמר.' You might have thought we should make a גזירה against a מאמר after חליצה because of a מאמר before חליצה (which does work). So the משנה teaches that we make no such גזירה. But why do I need 'he did חליצה and then gave a גט'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה for including a case that seems to teach nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מאמר before חליצה really works, so one might have thought חכמים would decree that a מאמר after חליצה also has some effect, so people don't confuse the two. That makes the מאמר case useful. A גט after חליצה, though, has no obvious reason to work, so the case looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted (accepting one part before attacking another)
It was needed (it teaches something)
You might have thought to say
Let us make a rabbinic decree (גזירה)
It teaches us
Why do I need it?

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the גט case is wrong. It is only asking why the משנה bothered to mention it.

phrases.english: Granted, 'he did חליצה and made a מאמר' was needed,
since you might have thought to say:
let us decree about a מאמר that comes after חליצה
because of a מאמר that comes before חליצה,
phrases.notes: A מאמר before חליצה does take effect, so the worry is that people would mix the two up.

phrases.english: so it teaches us that we do not decree.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא חָלַץ וְנָתַן גֵּט לְמָה לִי?
phrases.english: But 'he did חליצה and gave a גט,' why do I need it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the wording of the quoted משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's inclusion of the case of a גט after חליצה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Every case in a משנה should teach something. The מאמר case teaches that we make no גזירה, but the גט case seems to teach nothing.

steps.title: Counter-question: the בעילה cases have the same problem
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with a counter-question: the סיפא about בעילה also contains a case that seems unnecessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: And by your logic, look at the סיפא: 'he had relations and made a מאמר; he had relations and gave a גט.' It makes sense that 'relations and then a גט' was needed. You might have thought we should decree about a גט after בעילה because of a גט before בעילה, so the משנה teaches that we don't. But 'relations and then a מאמר,' why do I need that?
steps.whatsHappening: Instead of answering right away, the גמרא shows that the same question applies to the second half of the משנה too. This sets up the real answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גט before בעילה does not fully release her, so one might have thought a גט after בעילה is also not enough. That makes the גט case useful there. But a מאמר after בעילה is obviously pointless, since after בעילה she is already fully his wife. So whatever answer explains the extra case in the רישא must also explain the extra case in the סיפא.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning (a counter-question)
Say (look at) the latter part of the משנה
He had relations (performed יבום through בעילה)
Marital relations

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning, say the latter part:

phrases.aramaic: בָּעַל וְעָשָׂה מַאֲמָר, בָּעַל וְנָתַן גֵּט —
phrases.english: 'he had relations and made a מאמר; he had relations and gave a גט':
granted, 'he had relations and gave a גט' was needed,
since you might have thought to say:
let us decree about a גט that comes after בעילה
because of a גט that comes before בעילה,
phrases.notes: A גט before בעילה alone doesn't fully release her, so one might think the same about a גט after it.

phrases.english: so it teaches us that we do not decree;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בָּעַל וְעָשָׂה מַאֲמָר לְמָה לִי?
phrases.english: but 'he had relations and made a מאמר,' why do I need it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the question back by showing the parallel problem in the סיפא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that every case in the משנה must teach a new חידוש.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If extra cases are a problem, the סיפא has one too (מאמר after בעילה), so we need a broader explanation.

steps.title: The extra cases are listed only to keep the pattern parallel
steps.stepSummary: Some cases appear only because the משנה wanted its two halves to match.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: since it taught 'חליצה and then a מאמר,' it also taught 'בעילה and then a מאמר.' And since it wanted to teach 'בעילה and then a גט,' it also taught 'חליצה and then a גט.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real answer: the two unneeded cases are there only to make the lists match.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each half has one case with a real חידוש: מאמר after חליצה, and גט after בעילה. The other case in each half (גט after חליצה, מאמר after בעילה) was added only so the two halves would line up. So we should not try to learn a new law from those extra cases.

keyTerms.meaning: Since / because of (a case added only to match another)
He (the תנא) taught
To teach

steps.whatToRemember: The rule of אַיְּידֵי: a משנה sometimes includes a case with no new law just to keep its wording parallel. Each half here has one real חידוש and one 'matching' case.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא: אַיְּידֵי דִּתְנָא חָלַץ וְעָשָׂה מַאֲמָר,
phrases.english: Rather: since it taught 'he did חליצה and made a מאמר,'
it also taught 'he had relations and made a מאמר.'

phrases.aramaic: וְאַיְּידֵי דְבָעֵי לְמִיתְנֵי בָּעַל וְנָתַן גֵּט,
phrases.english: And since it wanted to teach 'he had relations and gave a גט,'
it also taught 'he did חליצה and gave a גט.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: אַיְּידֵי דִּתְנָא חָלַץ וְעָשָׂה מַאֲמָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves both the original question and the counter-question with one explanation.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Stylistic parallelism (אַיְּידֵי): the extra cases have no independent חידוש.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every case in the משנה must teach its own new law.
steps.terutzMaskana: The גט after חליצה and the מאמר after בעילה are listed only to match the other half of the משנה.

steps.title: Our משנה does not follow a certain תנא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line about בעילה 'when it is at the beginning' and says the משנה disagrees with another תנא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'When it (the בעילה) is at the beginning, etc.' Our משנה is not like this תנא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and states that it goes against a certain תנא. This sets up the ברייתא quoted in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says בעילה ends everything only if it came first, but חליצה ends everything at any stage. The גמרא is about to show a תנא who treats חליצה differently from our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: When it is (at the beginning)
Our משנה
A sage of the משנה period

phrases.english: 'When it is,' etc.
phrases.notes: The full line in the משנה: when the בעילה is first, nothing works after it; in the middle or at the end, something does.

phrases.english: Our משנה is not like this תנא,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line of the משנה and a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Our משנה disagrees with the תנא about to be quoted.

steps.title: The ברייתא of אבא יוסי בן יוחנן: חליצה is like בעילה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says that both בעילה and חליצה end everything only when they come first.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: אבא יוסי בן יוחנן, a man of ירושלים, says in the name of רבי מאיר: both בעילה and חליצה, if done at the beginning, nothing works after them. If done in the middle or at the end, something does work after them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that shows which תנא our משנה disagrees with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this ברייתא, חליצה works just like בעילה: it closes the door only if it was the first action. Our משנה instead says nothing works after חליצה no matter when it was done. So on חליצה, the משנה and the ברייתא disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
In the name of
At the beginning (the first action)
In the middle or at the end (after another action)
Nothing takes effect after it

steps.whatToRemember: Our משנה: חליצה ends everything at any stage, but בעילה does so only at the beginning. The ברייתא (אבא יוסי בן יוחנן in the name of רבי מאיר): both בעילה and חליצה end everything only at the beginning.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: אַבָּא יוֹסֵי בֶּן יוֹחָנָן אִישׁ יְרוּשָׁלַיִם
phrases.english: Abba Yosei ben Yochanan, a man of Jerusalem,
says in the name of Rabbi Meir:
both בעילה and חליצה:
at the beginning, nothing takes effect after it;
in the middle or at the end, something does take effect after it.
phrases.notes: 'In the middle or at the end' means some other action, like a מאמר or גט, came before it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: אַבָּא יוֹסֵי בֶּן יוֹחָנָן אִישׁ יְרוּשָׁלַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source showing the opposing תנא mentioned in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that our משנה does not follow this תנא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of אבא יוסי בן יוחנן in the name of רבי מאיר, which treats חליצה like בעילה.

steps.title: Three opinions, starting with the first תנא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sums up that there are three opinions. The תנא קמא decrees for ביאה but not for חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: So there are three opinions on this. The first תנא holds: with ביאה, where there is a reason to make a decree, we make one. With חליצה, where there is no reason to make a decree, we do not make one.
steps.whatsHappening: Using the ברייתא from the last step, the גמרא now lays out three opinions. It starts with the first תנא, who is the view of our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא says ביאה only finishes everything when it comes first. If it comes after a גט or מאמר, it does not. The reason is a decree, because there is something to worry about with ביאה. With חליצה there is nothing to worry about, so חליצה finishes everything wherever it comes.

keyTerms.meaning: Three opinions
The first, unnamed תנא
To make a rabbinic decree
We make a decree

phrases.english: And there are three opinions on the matter.
The first tanna holds:
Intercourse, where there is a reason to decree, we decree.
Chalitza, where there is no reason to decree, we do not decree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the ברייתא quoted in step 6
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The תנא קמא makes a decree only for ביאה, so ביאה ends everything only when it comes first, while חליצה ends everything anywhere.

steps.title: רבי נחמיה sees no need for any decree
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה says there is no need to decree even for ביאה, because people know how Torah-level acts work.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נחמיה holds that even with ביאה there is no reason to decree. You said we should decree on ביאה after a גט because of ביאה after חליצה. But חליצה is from the Torah, so people know its rule well. You also said we should decree on ביאה after a מאמר because of ביאה after ביאה. But ביאה is from the Torah, so this too is well known.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second opinion, רבי נחמיה. It answers each worry that led the תנא קמא to make a decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא feared people would mix up a rabbinic case with a Torah case. רבי נחמיה says Torah laws like חליצה and ביאה are famous, so nobody will confuse them. Without that fear there is no decree, and ביאה ends everything wherever it comes, just like חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who holds there is no decree at all
From the Torah
People surely know it
Rabbinic betrothal of a יבמה with money or a document

phrases.english: And Rabbi Nechemya holds:
With intercourse too, there is no reason to decree.
And as for what you said, that we should decree on
phrases.notes: רבי נחמיה is speaking to the תנא קמא as if face to face.

phrases.aramaic: בִּיאָה אַחַר הַגֵּט מִשּׁוּם בִּיאָה אַחַר חֲלִיצָה —
phrases.english: intercourse after a get because of intercourse after chalitza:
since chalitza is from the Torah, people surely know it.
And as for what you said, that we should decree on

phrases.aramaic: בִּיאָה אַחַר מַאֲמָר מִשּׁוּם בִּיאָה אַחַר בִּיאָה —
phrases.english: intercourse after maamar because of intercourse after intercourse:

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּבִיאָה דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא, הָא מִידָּע יְדִיעִי.
phrases.english: since intercourse is from the Torah, this is surely known.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second of the three opinions and rejects the תנא קמא's reasons for a decree
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No decree for ביאה or חליצה, because Torah-level laws are well known and will not be confused.

steps.title: אבא יוסי בן חנן decrees for both
steps.stepSummary: אבא יוסי בן חנן agrees there is a decree for ביאה and adds a decree for חליצה because of ביאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא יוסי בן חנן agrees with the רבנן who decree about ביאה. He also decrees about חליצה because of ביאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the third opinion, the opposite of רבי נחמיה. It finishes the list of three views.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He starts from the same decree on ביאה as the תנא קמא. Then he goes further and treats חליצה the same way, so the two do not look different. That is why, for him, both ביאה and חליצה end everything only when they come first.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who decrees for both ביאה and חליצה
The Sages, here the תנא קמא

steps.whatToRemember: There are three views. The תנא קמא decrees for ביאה only. רבי נחמיה makes no decree at all. אבא יוסי בן חנן decrees for both ביאה and חליצה.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַבָּא יוֹסֵי בֶּן חָנָן סָבַר לַהּ
phrases.english: And Abba Yosei ben Chanan holds
like the Rabbis, who decree about intercourse,
and he decrees about chalitza because of intercourse.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַבָּא יוֹסֵי בֶּן חָנָן סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the third opinion and completes the list of three
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a decree for both ביאה and חליצה, so each ends everything only when it comes first.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק רבן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula of the פרק רבן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק רבן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the פרק. It is not part of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is a traditional goodbye to a פרק we have finished, with the hope of coming back to learn it again. Nothing in the halacha changes here.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you, said when finishing a פרק

phrases.english: We will return to you, Rabban Gamliel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק after the final sugya
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פרק רבן גמליאל is finished.

steps.title: Any act of ביאה acquires the יבמה
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that ביאה with a יבמה acquires her in every case. It does not matter whether either side meant it or was forced, or whether the act was only begun.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a man has ביאה with his יבמה, he acquires her. This is true whether he did it by mistake or on purpose, whether he was forced or willing. It is true even if he was mistaken and she acted on purpose, or he acted on purpose and she was mistaken. It is true if he was forced and she was not, or she was forced and he was not. It is the same whether he only began the act or finished it. And there is no difference between one kind of ביאה and another.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק opens with a משנה. It teaches that ביאה with a יבמה works to acquire her even without proper intent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the Torah's acquisition of a יבמה through ביאה works no matter what was in anyone's mind. It works with mistakes and with force on either side. Even the first stage of the act is enough, and an unusual way of ביאה counts too.

keyTerms.meaning: One who has ביאה with his יבמה
By mistake / on purpose
Forced / willing
One who only begins the act
One who completes the act
He has acquired her

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'by mistake' does not mean the act failed. It means he did not intend יבום, for example because he did not know she was his יבמה. The act still acquires her.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic rule for the whole new פרק. In יבום, the Torah's acquisition through ביאה does not depend on intent.

phrases.english: One who has intercourse with his yevama,
whether unwittingly or intentionally,
whether forced or willingly,
even if he was unwitting and she was intentional,
he was intentional and she was unwitting,
he was forced and she was not forced,
she was forced and he was not forced.
Both one who begins the act and one who completes it has acquired her.
And it did not distinguish between one intercourse and another.
phrases.notes: This means the normal way and an unusual way of ביאה count the same.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַבָּא עַל יְבִמְתּוֹ, בֵּין בְּשׁוֹגֵג בֵּין בְּמֵזִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new פרק after the הדרן
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any ביאה with a יבמה acquires her, regardless of intent, force, or whether the act was completed, and in either manner of ביאה.

steps.title: The same rule for forbidden and disqualified relations
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends by extending its rule. Someone who has relations with an ערוה or with a woman who is פסולה to him disqualifies her, and no distinction is made between one kind of ביאה and another.
steps.simpleTranslation: Likewise, if someone has relations with any of the forbidden relatives in the Torah, or with a woman who is disqualified to him, he has disqualified her. Examples are a widow with a כהן גדול, a divorcee or חלוצה with a regular כהן, a ממזרת or נתינה with a regular Jew, or a Jewish woman with a ממזר or נתין. The Torah made no distinction between one kind of ביאה and another.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is finishing its list. It says the 'any kind of ביאה counts' rule also applies to forbidden and disqualified relations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a יבמה, any ביאה acquires her. Here the משנה says the same is true on the negative side. Any ביאה with an ערוה or a פסולה makes her disqualified, whether or not he meant it. The common thread is that the act itself counts, not the person's intention.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden relationships listed in the Torah
Women who are disqualified from marrying a certain man (for example, a divorcee to a כהן)
A regular כהן, not the כהן גדול
A descendant of the Givonim, who may not marry into the general Jewish community
He disqualified her

phrases.english: And likewise, one who has relations with one
of all the forbidden relatives in the Torah,
or with women who are disqualified to him,
such as a widow with a high priest,
a divorcee or a woman released by חליצה with a regular priest,
a ממזרת or a נתינה with a regular Jew,
a Jewish woman with a ממזר or a נתין
he has disqualified her
phrases.notes: Because of this act, she becomes disqualified, for example from marrying a כהן.

phrases.english: And no distinction was made between one kind of relations and another.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן הַבָּא עַל אַחַת מִכׇּל הָעֲרָיוֹת שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה that began in step 11, applying the same 'any ביאה counts' idea to עריות and פסולות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any ביאה with an ערוה or a פסולה disqualifies her, regardless of intent or kind of ביאה.

steps.title: Why does the משנה say 'even'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking what the word 'אפילו' in the משנה is adding.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the point of the word 'even'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה. It asks why the משנה said 'even if he was unwitting and she was intentional.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already said intent makes no difference. So adding 'even' for one specific case seems unnecessary. The גמרא wants to know what this case adds that we did not already know.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
Even

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is the point of 'even'?
phrases.notes: The משנה said 'even if he was unwitting and she acted on purpose.' The גמרא wants to know why that case is special.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא's first question on the משנה's wording.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does 'אפילו' add, if the משנה already said intent does not matter?

steps.title: The משנה is building from easy cases to a harder one
steps.stepSummary: The משנה uses a 'לא מיבעיא' style. Obviously he acquires her when at least she intends the מצוה. But even when neither of them intends the מצוה, he still acquires her.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is speaking in the style of 'it goes without saying.' It goes without saying that he acquires her if he is unwitting and she intends the מצוה. The same is true if he acts on purpose and she intends the מצוה. But even if he is unwitting and she acts on purpose, so that neither of them intends the מצוה, he still acquires her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'even' marks the most surprising case. That is the case where neither person is thinking about the מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the easier cases, at least the woman meant the מצוה, so acquiring makes sense. 'אפילו' points to the case where nobody had the מצוה in mind. Even there, the ביאה still works.

keyTerms.meaning: It goes without saying. A style that moves from an obvious case to a bigger one
Acting without knowing (unwitting)
Acting on purpose
For the sake of the מצוה
He acquired her (she becomes his wife)

steps.whatToRemember: With יבום, the act of ביאה acquires the יבמה even if neither side has the מצוה in mind.

phrases.english: It is speaking in the style of 'it goes without saying.'
It goes without saying when he is unwitting
and she intends to do the מצוה,
or also when he acts on purpose
and she intends to do the מצוה,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ הוּא שׁוֹגֵג וְהִיא מְזִידָה,
phrases.english: but even when he is unwitting and she acts on purpose,
phrases.notes: 'On purpose' here means she knows what she is doing, but she is not doing it for the מצוה.

phrases.english: where neither of them intends it for the sake of the מצוה,
even so, he acquires her.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'אפילו' introduces the most surprising case, where neither side intends the מצוה, and he still acquires her.

steps.title: רבי חייא's ברייתא goes even further
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא taught that he acquires her even when both are unwitting, both act on purpose, or both are forced.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא taught: Even if both of them are unwitting, both act on purpose, or both are forced, he acquires her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא from רבי חייא that widens the משנה's rule to more cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה listed cases where at least one side was unwitting or forced. רבי חייא adds cases where both sides are in the same state: both unwitting, both on purpose, or both forced. In every one of these, the ביאה still acquires her.

keyTerms.meaning: Taught (introduces a ברייתא)
Forced, done against their will

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya taught:
Even if both of them are unwitting,
both act on purpose, or both are forced.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ברייתא that continues and widens the explanation in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ביאה acquires the יבמה even when both are unwitting, both act on purpose, or both are forced.

steps.title: What case of a 'forced' man does the משנה mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what situation the משנה means when it says the man was אנוס (forced).
steps.simpleTranslation: The 'forced' man in our משנה: what is the case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It asks what kind of 'forced' man the משנה could mean.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the ביאה counts even if he was forced. Before accepting this, the גמרא wants to picture a real case where a man is truly forced into relations.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who acts under force or against his will
What is the case? How does it look?

phrases.english: The forced man of our mishna, what are the circumstances?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the word 'אפילו' to the term 'אנוס' in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What realistic case of a man being forced does the משנה have in mind?

steps.title: It cannot mean that non-Jews forced him
steps.stepSummary: The first suggestion is that non-Jews forced him to have relations. It is challenged by רבא's rule that a man cannot truly be forced into forbidden relations, since an erection needs his own will.
steps.simpleTranslation: Suppose you say it is when non-Jews forced him and he had relations with her. But didn't רבא say that there is no such thing as being forced into forbidden relations, since there is no erection without intent?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the obvious answer, that non-Jews forced him, and immediately challenges it using רבא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא holds that a man's physical arousal shows he is acting willingly, even under threat. So 'forced by non-Jews' is not really forced at all. That means the גמרא still needs a different case to explain what the משנה meant by אנוס.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a suggestion that will be rejected)
But didn't (he) say? (introduces a challenge)
There is no being forced for forbidden relations
Erection
With intent, willingly

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the threat never happened. He is saying that because an erection only happens willingly, the act itself counts as done with intent, so it does not fit the משנה's word 'forced.'

phrases.english: If you say it is when non-Jews forced him
and he had relations with her,
but didn't Rava say:
There is no coercion for forbidden relations!
Because there is no erection without intent.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא כְּשֶׁאֲנָסוּהוּ גּוֹיִם וּבָא עָלֶיהָ, וְהָאָמַר רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to step 16 and challenges it right away.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the משנה's אנוס is a man threatened by non-Jews.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא rules that an erection only happens willingly, so a threatened man is not truly forced. This case therefore cannot be the משנה's אנוס.

steps.title: Second suggestion: the man was asleep
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the משנה's 'forced' case means the man was asleep.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the משנה is talking about a man who was asleep.
steps.whatsHappening: The first explanation of 'forced' was knocked down, so the גמרא offers a new one. Maybe the man was asleep when it happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's rule said a man who has relations cannot truly be forced, because an erection needs his will. A sleeping man avoids that problem, since he did not choose anything at all. So sleeping could count as a real case of אונס.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; signals that the earlier answer is dropped and a new one is given
A sleeping person

phrases.english: Rather, it is a case of one who is asleep.
phrases.notes: This answers the question from step 16: what does the משנה mean by 'forced'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer rejected in step 17 with a new case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What case counts as 'forced' in the משנה

steps.title: Starting a challenge from רב יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to challenge the 'asleep' answer by bringing a statement of רב יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is about to quote רב יהודה to challenge the idea that the man was asleep; his actual words come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'וְהָא' tells us a challenge is coming. The גמרא is hinting that רב יהודה said something that does not fit with the 'asleep' case. We need the next line to see exactly what the problem is.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't [so-and-so] say? Opens a challenge from a known statement
An אמורא whose statement is about to be quoted

steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for the challenge in this line itself. It only names who is being quoted; the actual problem is in his words that follow.

phrases.english: But didn't Rav Yehuda say:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a challenge against the 'asleep' answer of step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the 'forced' case is a sleeping man
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A statement of רב יהודה, quoted next, apparently conflicts with the 'asleep' case.
